A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe the same SpeechIQ research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite the revised title.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations across three speech datasets, human-ranking comparisons, and hallucination analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, human-evaluation, and hallucination results, including the detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Figure 2 retain the same remember/understand/apply evaluation pipeline, embedding similarity, QA procedure, and SIQ aggregation. The title's addition of 'Agentic' introduces no method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Earning22 financial speech, VoxPopuli parliamentary speech, and Medical-ASR-EN medical speech. The human evaluations and unanswerable-question scenario are also retained without coverage changes.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 4 retain the same cascaded and end-to-end systems. Table 3 retains WER, SemDist, LLM-S, BLEU, and both SIQ variants; Table 7 retains the Qwen2-7B versus GPT-4o comparison.

E3.justification: The longest-audio subsets remain 200 Earning22, 200 VoxPopuli, and 400 medical samples. Both versions retain three questions with five choices per sample, the same model configurations, and the same human-evaluation designs.

E4.justification: The matched-foundation-model comparison, use of end-to-end models to supply cascaded transcriptions, human comparisons, and unanswerable-set analysis are unchanged. Appendices B and C retain the same answering-model validation and hallucination case studies.

E5.justification: Table 2 still reports single experiments for remember/understand and majority voting over five QA generations. Table 3 retains the same Spearman correlations and p-values. No seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Scores, rankings, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. Examples include SIQ 108.64 for Whisper-v2 + GPT-4o + Qwen2 in Table 2 and SIQall's human-ranking correlation of 0.952 in Table 3. Appendix D's per-dataset plots are identical.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same similarity definitions, discrimination weights, standardization, and SIQ transformation. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof changes; Appendix E retains the same discussion of future scaling normalization.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about three-level cognitive evaluation, comparison across architectures, annotation-error identification, and hallucination detection. The revised title does not substantively extend these contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning modality interference, inherited hallucinations, and scaling remain unchanged. The limitations still cover dataset size, leakage, missing scaling normalization, ethical concerns, and unexplored upper Bloom levels; the introductory wording edit adds no substantive qualification.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B retain the same prompts, QA-validation instructions, and default-model-setting disclosure. The leaderboard and dataset access information and promise of future code/data release are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, and positioning relative to transcription metrics, semantic metrics, and voice-model architectures remain unchanged. Reference spacing and reflow do not change the bibliography's substantive content.

P1.justification: The title changes 'Speech Intelligence' to 'Speech-Agentic Intelligence' and adds 'by' before 'Large Language Models.' The limitations introduction changes 'our study has limitations' to the ungrammatical 'our study limits.' The section organization and remaining substantive prose are retained.

P2.justification: Small caption and heading spacing changes accompany modest reflow on pages 9–10, moving the closing limitations line onto page 9 and shifting acknowledgements/references. Figure and table designs are retained; the appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v2 retains the same scientific contribution, empirical support, limitations, and reproducibility information. The title and modest presentation edits introduce no substantive improvement, while the isolated grammatical regression in the limitations introduction is too limited to meaningfully change overall paper quality.
